result.note: Tests the US tariff and sanctions history behind India's Venezuelan crude imports and India's rank among buyers in May 2026; the visit itself and the trade-leverage analysis are skipped.

questions.prompt: Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez visited India in June 2026. Consider the following statements about India's imports of Venezuelan crude oil:
items: India halted Venezuelan purchases in 2025 after the US imposed a 50% tariff on countries buying Venezuelan crude.
India's imports resumed in February 2026 after Washington eased sanctions following the capture of Nicolás Maduro.
Under the current arrangement, the US Treasury controls the proceeds and sets the commercial terms.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the US tariff that led India to halt purchases in 2025 was 25%, not 50%. Imports resumed in February 2026 once sanctions eased, with the US Treasury holding the proceeds.
questions.source: India halted Venezuelan purchases last year after Washington imposed a 25% tariff on countries buying Venezuelan crude.

questions.prompt: In May 2026, India imported 427,000 barrels per day of Venezuelan crude and became its second-largest buyer. Which country was the largest buyer?
questions.explain: India's May 2026 purchases were second only to those of the US. With the West Asia crisis blocking 40% of India's usual crude imports, Venezuela became a distant but important source of supply.
questions.source: In May, India gobbled up 427,000 barrels per day, second only to the US.
